title: Pendulum

source.credit: Rendered by Ansatz with exactly known physics (L = 0.80 m, released at 70°)

slow_motion.evidence: no narration, captions or on-screen text indicate slow motion; animation plays as continuous pendulum motion

subjects.description: small shiny blue spherical pendulum bob suspended by a thin string from a fixed pivot

observation.what_happens: A blue ball suspended by a thin string swings side to side from a fixed pivot. It starts held high on the right, then swings freely through the bottom to the left and back repeatedly until the clip ends.

calibration.note: no ruler needed: the swing is measured as an angle

given: g = 9.807 m/s² (Earth): hold g fixed and measure the pendulum's length L in metres from its swing
reasoning: The path is circular to 0.15 px and theta spans +-1.2 rad with period near 2 s and peaks decaying from 1.22 to 1.01 rad. Candidates test small-angle vs large-angle restoring torque and no loss vs linear viscous loss vs quadratic air drag, all with g fixed so L is determined by timing.

law.title: Damped Pendulum with Linear Friction
law.summary: A circular swing that slowly loses energy to a friction that grows with swing speed.

params.name: L
params.meaning: pendulum length from pivot to centre of ball

params.name: gamma
params.meaning: viscous damping rate from pivot friction and slow air drag

caveats: Length in metres rests entirely on assumed Earth gravity with no independent scale.
Pivot is assumed perfectly still with a rigid massless string.
critique.finding: It swings on a string of length {L} pulled down by gravity {g}. Each swing shrinks a little from gentle friction {gamma}.
critique.headline: The swinging ball fades slowly from gentle air friction
critique.why_it_won: It captures the steady fade of all swings while quadratic drag shrinks large swings too quickly and small swings too slowly.

headline: The swinging ball fades slowly from gentle air friction
finding: It swings on a string of length 0.8 ± 2.93e-5 m pulled down by gravity 9.81 m/s^2. Each swing shrinks a little from gentle friction 0.0601 ± 9.26e-5 1/s.

eyeball.confidence: medium for L, low for gamma
eyeball.law_in_words: simple pendulum small-angle motion theta-double-dot + gamma theta-dot + (g/L) theta = 0, so period T = 2pi sqrt(L/g) and amplitude envelope decays as exp(-gamma t/2)
